slots.title: September CPI due Tuesday with 3.7% YoY est.
slots.body:
Headline CPI for September is expected at 3.7% year over year, up from 3.4% in the prior month.

Core inflation—the slice that strips out volatile food and energy—is estimated at 2.5% YoY vs 2.4% previously, with a 0.2% month-over-month core read vs 0.3% last time.

The release is scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 14, at 12:30 p.m.
ET alongside CPI n.s.a and Cleveland CPI readings.

What part of the CPI report do you watch first—headline, core, or shelter?

slots.title: IMF sees 3.1% global growth in 2026
slots.body:
The IMF’s updated outlook puts 2026 global growth at 3.1%, down from 3.5% but above the 3.0% figure it had in July.

The fund cited AI-related investment and fiscal support as offsets to war-related drag.

It also expects inflation at 4.7% this year with energy costs still elevated, then 4.1% in 2027.

Which line matters more for your read on rates—inflation at 4.7% or growth holding above the July estimate?

slots.title: U.S. cash session — Oct. 13, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,850.55, up +0.4% (+195.60 points), while the S&P 500 ended at 7,807.24, down −0.1% (−4.30 points).

The Nasdaq Composite finished at 27,245.90, down −0.4% (−120.27 points); the Russell 2000 closed at 2,794.48, down −0.4% (−12.50 points).

The CBOE Volatility Index rose to 15.21, up +2.5% (+0.37 point), from a prior close of 14.84.

On the calendar for the session, the U.S. had high-impact housing releases scheduled for 2:00 p.m.
ET: Existing Home Sales (Sep), estimated at 3.96M with a prior reading of 3.98M, and Existing Home Sales month-over-month (Sep), estimated at −0.3% with a prior reading of −2.0%.

Earnings were scheduled the same day for several large financial and consumer names, including $JPM, $GS, $WFC, $C, $JNJ, $UNH, $DPZ, and $ACI; the injected data lists estimates only, not reported results.

$META led among highlighted megacaps, closing at 742.96, up +3.4% (+24.29); $MSFT rose +1.1% to 541.15 and $AAPL gained +1.3% to 340.97.

Semiconductor and software heavies were weaker: $NVDA −1.3% to 226.32, $AMD −2.3% to 594.24, $TSM −2.0% to 444.35, $AVGO −1.9% to 354.73, and $ORCL −2.8% to 137.40.

Consumer and internet megacaps also slipped: $AMZN −1.1% to 259.53 and $TSLA −1.2% to 378.03.

Energy majors finished higher: $XOM +1.9% to 172.15 and $CVX +1.4% to 215.00.

Among banks on the earnings slate, $C closed +1.8% at 131.93, $JPM +0.4% at 334.30, $GS −0.2% at 893.95, and $WFC −0.3% at 83.30.

Sector averages on Nasdaq showed Real Estate up about +1.6%, Communication Services about +1.0%, and Consumer Defensive about +1.0%, while Technology averaged about −0.8% and Utilities about −1.1%.

Overseas, Japan’s Nikkei 225 closed at 67,637.77, down −2.0% (−1,393.15 points); the FTSE 100 rose +1.0% to 10,656.28.

Gold futures settled at 4,224.00, up +0.8% (+33.40).
The United States Oil Fund (USO) closed at 151.03, up +1.9% (+2.83), while Brent crude (BZUSD) was at 105.31, down −1.3% (−1.34).

The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund (UUP) closed at 29.13, up +0.4% (+0.11).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was at 83,697.86, up +2.4% (+1,943.38).

The latest Treasury snapshot in the data (dated 2026-10-09) showed the 10-year yield at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.44 percentage point.
